dose.text: GHK‑Cu coating To coat PCL–Col–Chit scaffolds with GHK-Cu, a solution of peptide in milli-Q water with a concentration of 1 mM was prepared and stirred at 4ºC for 2 h.

endpoint.text: The absorbance was measured at 570 nm by ELISA plate reader (Biotek-Epoch, USA).

reported_results.text: Compared to poly(ε-caprolactone)/collagen/chitosan, the cell proliferation of GHK-Cu and bioactive glass-coated (concentrations of 0.01 and 0.1) scaffolds increased significantly at days 3 and 7, respectively.
A p value < 0.05 was considered as statistically significant.

There was not any difference between BG-coated samples and uncoated sample after 5 days, but substantial improvement was observed in BG-0.01 and BG-0.1 scaffolds on day 7 in comparison with the uncoated sample.

numbers.text: GHK‑Cu coating To coat PCL–Col–Chit scaffolds with GHK-Cu, a solution of peptide in milli-Q water with a concentration of 1 mM was prepared and stirred at 4ºC for 2 h.
The absorbance was measured at 570 nm by ELISA plate reader (Biotek-Epoch, USA).

MTT Assay The cell viability of samples was assessed using MTT assay [3-(4,5- dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5 diphenyltetrazolium bromide] by counting the number of human dermal fibroblast (HDF) (primary cell line, passage 2, cryopreserved) cultured on samples.

Compared to poly(ε-caprolactone)/collagen/chitosan, the cell proliferation of GHK-Cu and bioactive glass-coated (concentrations of 0.01 and 0.1) scaffolds increased significantly at days 3 and 7, respectively.
A p value < 0.05 was considered as statistically significant.

There was not any difference between BG-coated samples and uncoated sample after 5 days, but substantial improvement was observed in BG-0.01 and BG-0.1 scaffolds on day 7 in comparison with the uncoated sample.
